note: Complete public scientific-checker bank. Inactive unless SCIBENCH_TRIGGER_LOG is set. Historical quality-review metadata does not remove checker IDs from the agent-visible task.

checkers.alarm: the local spherical residual hypot(separation_error, |sin(separation)|*wrapped_position_angle_error) exceeds 10*eps64/min(|cos(lat1)|,|cos(lat2)|)^2
checkers.invariant: position_angle and separation measured from the produced endpoint must recover the position_angle and separation requested by directional_offset_by
checkers.observation_point: inside directional_offset_by, immediately after computing the new point, before returning it
checkers.precondition: canonical positive separation in [1e-6, pi-1e-6], and neither endpoint within |cos(lat)| < 1e-3 of a celestial pole
checkers.rationale: the docstrings of position_angle, separation, and directional_offset_by explicitly state they are inverse operations; a violation breaks that documented mathematical relationship
checkers.scientific_quantity: position on the celestial sphere reached by a directional offset

checkers.alarm: angular_separation between the original and round-tripped point exceeds 30*eps64
checkers.invariant: a chain of orthogonal rotation matrices composed with their inverses returns the identity transform up to float64 round-off
checkers.observation_point: inside transform_to, immediately after the composed transform is applied, before returning the result
checkers.precondition: transform_to call resolving to the same equivalent frame class through only static/dynamic matrix transforms; unit-spherical data, or distance-bearing Cartesian components with magnitude in [1e-150,1e150] so norm/conversion arithmetic remains representable
checkers.rationale: every coordinate conversion and catalog cross-match in astropy relies on these matrices being mutually consistent inverses; a violation indicates an error in a precession/frame-bias matrix or the transform graph's composition logic
checkers.scientific_quantity: angular position of a coordinate transformed around a closed loop of pure-rotation frame transforms

checkers.alarm: relative error in 3D Cartesian norm between original and round-tripped vector exceeds 30*eps64
checkers.invariant: a pure rotation preserves vector norm and pairwise structure, so the round-tripped Cartesian vector equals the original up to float64 round-off, relative to the vector's own magnitude
checkers.observation_point: inside transform_to, immediately after the composed transform is applied, before returning the result
checkers.precondition: same as AP-COORD-002, restricted to distance-bearing coordinates with finite Cartesian component magnitude in [1e-150,1e150]
checkers.rationale: same as AP-COORD-002, assigned to the same root-cause family since both observe the identical underlying matrix-composition error from a single transform_to call
checkers.scientific_quantity: 3D Cartesian position of a distance-bearing coordinate transformed around a closed loop of pure-rotation frame transforms

checkers.alarm: separation(A,C) - (separation(A,B) + separation(B,C)) exceeds 10*eps64, where B is derived deterministically from A and C (arbitrary point off the A-C geodesic, not a degenerate/collinear special case)
checkers.invariant: separation(A, C) <= separation(A, B) + separation(B, C) for any three points A, B, C on the sphere
checkers.observation_point: inside separation(A, C), immediately after angular_separation(A, C) is computed
checkers.precondition: none -- the triangle inequality for a metric holds unconditionally, including at coincident points, poles, and antipodes
checkers.rationale: if the triangle inequality fails, angular_separation is not computing a proper metric, which would break nearest-neighbor search, catalog matching, and clustering algorithms that implicitly rely on it
checkers.scientific_quantity: great-circle (geodesic) distance between two points on the celestial sphere

checkers.alarm: abs((round_tripped - original).sec) exceeds 5e-11 seconds
checkers.invariant: a single scale conversion must be its own inverse when immediately reversed -- every pairwise conversion in the analytic (non-UT1) subset of MULTI_HOPS is an exactly invertible relation; a multi-hop loop reduces to this hop-by-hop
checkers.observation_point: inside Time.__getattr__, immediately after a new-scale Time replica is constructed and cached, before it is returned
checkers.precondition: scalar, unmasked Time with |JD|<=1e8; UT1 excluded; UTC-involving conversions additionally restricted to the loaded leap-second table validity range
checkers.rationale: every physical-time calculation in astropy (light-travel-time corrections, barycentric corrections, sidereal time, ephemeris lookups) depends on scale conversions being mutually consistent inverses to sub-microsecond precision
checkers.scientific_quantity: an instant in time (epoch) re-expressed across time scales (TAI, TT, TCG, TCB, TDB, UTC)

checkers.alarm: abs((reconstructed - T2).sec) exceeds 5e-11 seconds
checkers.invariant: Time.__sub__ and Time.__add__ form an additive group action: T1 + (T2 - T1) must equal T2 for any two valid epochs
checkers.observation_point: inside Time.__sub__, in the T-T branch, immediately after the resulting TimeDelta is finalized, before it is returned
checkers.precondition: T1, T2 both scalar, unmasked Time instances with |JD| <= 1e8; same leap-second-table validity restriction as AP-TIME-001 when either is UTC-involving. The JD bound keeps fixed-epoch rate conversions inside the 50-ps float64 error model.
checkers.rationale: light-curve folding, orbit propagation, and any time-grid construction via repeated TimeDelta addition relies on this exact inverse relationship
checkers.scientific_quantity: elapsed duration between two epochs, and the epoch reached by advancing from a given epoch by a given duration

checkers.alarm: Euclidean pixel distance between the original pixel and wcs_world2pix(world) exceeds 1e-6 pixels
checkers.invariant: wcs_pix2world and wcs_world2pix are documented as mutual inverses on the core projection
checkers.observation_point: inside wcs_pix2world, immediately after computing world coordinates, before returning them
checkers.precondition: finite pixel/world coordinates, non-facet-based projection (excludes CSC/TSC/QSC/HPX). Fixed 2026-09-15 (codex CLI black-box trial): the tolerance is now scaled by pixel coordinate magnitude (max(1, max|original_xy|)) -- previously a flat 1e-6px absolute bound, calibrated against realistic (+/-2000px) coordinates, trivially failed at pixel ~1e14 (needs >20 significant digits regardless of wcslib's actual accuracy). This was a checker precondition gap, not a wcslib defect.
checkers.rationale: every WCS-based coordinate lookup (aperture photometry, image reprojection, catalog cross-matching) assumes this round trip holds; a violation means the compiled wcslib extension and its Python wrapper have drifted out of sync, or wcslib itself has a projection-specific defect
checkers.scientific_quantity: a pixel location re-expressed as a world coordinate via the core wcslib projection (no SIP/distortion), and back

checkers.alarm: pixel_distance(original, all_world2pix_result) exceeds 10 * the explicit 1e-4 tolerance used by the checker re-call
checkers.invariant: when the checker re-calls all_world2pix at its default tolerance and it returns without raising NoConvergence, the pixel distance to the true originating pixel must not exceed that default tolerance by more than a small, derived safety margin
checkers.observation_point: inside all_pix2world, immediately after computing world coordinates, re-calling all_world2pix at its own default tolerance and comparing to the original pixel
checkers.precondition: any world coordinate produced by all_pix2world from a pixel within all_world2pix's convergence domain -- i.e. any call that returns without raising NoConvergence
checkers.rationale: all_world2pix is the standard API for converting catalog sky positions back to detector pixels under real SIP-distorted optics; if it silently returns a pixel farther than its documented tolerance promises, every downstream photometric aperture or catalog cross-match is silently degraded with no warning
checkers.scientific_quantity: a pixel location recovered by iterative numerical inversion of the full (SIP+distortion-inclusive) forward transform, and the accuracy with which that inversion achieves its own documented convergence contract

checkers.alarm: relative round-trip error in wavelength exceeds 5*eps64
checkers.invariant: spectral()'s three pairwise conversions (m<->Hz, m<->J, Hz<->J) must be mutually consistent since all three encode the same c and h: wavelength -> frequency -> energy -> wavelength via three different pairwise entries must recover the original wavelength
checkers.observation_point: inside spectral(), on the equivalency list it is about to return, by extracting and composing the raw conversion functions directly (not by observing a live Quantity.to() call, since that machinery is fully generic and used by every unit conversion in astropy)
checkers.precondition: any wavelength lambda > 0 -- the full physically meaningful range, no upper/lower bound
checkers.rationale: spectral() is the standard equivalency for moving between wavelength/frequency/energy representations of spectra; a violation would mean h or c, or the conversion formulas, are inconsistent between the three pairwise conversions
checkers.scientific_quantity: wavelength, frequency, and energy of light, related by E=hf and f=c/lambda

checkers.alarm: the signed relative disagreement differs from -beta/2 + beta^2/2 by more than 1e-6
checkers.invariant: the two conventions are not claimed to agree exactly, but their leading-order disagreement is analytically derivable: beta_radio/beta -> 1 - beta/2 as beta -> 0
checkers.observation_point: inside doppler_radio(), re-calling the public doppler_relativistic() for the same rest frequency at signed redshift and blueshift probes spanning the beta precondition window
checkers.precondition: rest frequency magnitude in [16*sqrt(float64_min_normal), sqrt(float64_max)/16], and |beta| in (1e-5,1e-3); the frequency bound keeps squared ratios out of subnormal underflow/overflow
checkers.rationale: radio astronomers routinely switch between conventions depending on instrument/pipeline legacy; if the documented leading-order relationship breaks down even where it should hold, downstream velocity calibrations silently diverge from the claimed physics
checkers.scientific_quantity: radial velocity inferred from a Doppler-shifted spectral line, under the radio vs. relativistic naming conventions

checkers.alarm: abs(v_from_relativistic - v_from_redshift) / c exceeds 10*eps64
checkers.invariant: converting the same physical shift through each independent formula (frequency-ratio vs. redshift) must recover the same velocity
checkers.observation_point: inside doppler_relativistic(), re-calling the public doppler_redshift() at a redshift independently derived from the same frequency ratio, at several probe velocities spanning the domain
checkers.precondition: rest frequency magnitude in [16*sqrt(float64_min_normal), sqrt(float64_max)/16], and |beta| in (0,1); both exact formulas must remain in normal float64 arithmetic
checkers.rationale: redshift is the primary observable in extragalactic astronomy while frequency-ratio Doppler tracking is standard for stellar/planetary radial velocities; if these two descriptions disagree, one of the two independently-coded formulas has an error
checkers.scientific_quantity: radial velocity corresponding to a relativistic Doppler shift, expressed as a frequency ratio vs. as a redshift z -- two independently implemented code paths for the same formula

checkers.alarm: abs((T_bright/T_thermo - 1) - (-x^2/12)) exceeds 1e-6
checkers.invariant: the two temperature scales differ only by the Planck correction factor f(x) = x^2*e^x/(e^x-1)^2, whose small-x expansion is f(x) = 1 - x^2/12 + x^4/240 - ...
checkers.observation_point: inside thermodynamic_temperature(), re-calling the public brightness_temperature() for the same frequency on a synthetic test surface brightness
checkers.precondition: x = h*nu/(k*T_cmb) in (0, 0.1) -- the regime where the omitted x^4/240 Taylor term stays below the tolerance floor
checkers.rationale: CMB and radio-astronomy pipelines routinely choose between the two temperature scales depending on frequency band; if they disagree by more than the physically predicted correction, one of the two formulas or their physical constants has an inconsistency
checkers.scientific_quantity: temperature inferred from spectral surface brightness under the Rayleigh-Jeans approximation vs. the full Planck correction

checkers.alarm: for any (i,j) where the matrix is False, the central-difference derivative of output i w.r.t. input j at any of three deterministic probe points exceeds 1e-8
checkers.invariant: wherever separability_matrix[i,j] is False (output i structurally cannot depend on input j), the numerical central-difference partial derivative of output i w.r.t. input j must be exactly zero at any evaluation point; the reverse implication (True implies nonzero derivative) is NOT claimed, since separability_matrix is a deliberately conservative upper bound
checkers.observation_point: inside separability_matrix, immediately after computing the boolean matrix, before returning it
checkers.precondition: any compound model whose separability_matrix computes successfully (sub-models must have a defined .separable property), at any point where the model itself evaluates successfully
checkers.rationale: separability_matrix is a public API for downstream fitting frameworks and gwcs-style tooling to decide which model outputs can be evaluated or fit independently; an unsound analysis could cause a consumer to silently fit or cache the wrong sub-model
checkers.scientific_quantity: whether one output of a compound model can depend on a given input -- a structural property computed by walking the model's composition tree, independent of evaluating the model at any point

checkers.alarm: relative error between inv_efunc(z) and _inv_efunc_scalar(z) exceeds 20*eps64*max(1,sum(abs(E2_terms))/abs(sum(E2_terms)))
checkers.invariant: inv_efunc(z) (public, vectorized, pure-Python) and _inv_efunc_scalar(z, *_inv_efunc_scalar_args) (compiled Cython fast-path used internally as the quad() integrand) are two independently written implementations of the identical closed-form E(z)^-1 formula and must agree
checkers.observation_point: inside inv_efunc, immediately after computing the result, for scalar z
checkers.precondition: any FLRW subclass and scalar z>=0 for which both implementations and the four E(z)^2 component terms are finite/nonzero, with component-sum condition <= eps64^-1/2
checkers.rationale: _inv_efunc_scalar is the integrand for essentially every distance/age/lookback-time calculation via quad(), while inv_efunc is the public user-facing API for the same quantity; a violation means the compiled fast-path and the public method have drifted out of sync
checkers.scientific_quantity: the dimensionless Hubble-parameter-scaling function E(z)^-1, the core kernel of every Friedmann-equation-based distance/time/volume calculation

checkers.alarm: abs((age(0) - age(z)) - lookback_time(z)) exceeds 3 * 1.49e-8 * hubble_time (in the same unit, e.g. Gyr)
checkers.invariant: age(0) - age(z) = lookback_time(z), a consequence of integrating the same integrand (_lookback_time_integrand_scalar) over complementary bounds via scipy.integrate.quad
checkers.observation_point: inside lookback_time, re-calling the public age() at 0 and at z
checkers.precondition: any FLRW cosmology instance and scalar redshift z >= 0 for which age(0), age(z), and lookback_time(z) all converge
checkers.rationale: age and lookback_time are standard tools for converting between redshift and cosmic time; if they disagree with the age-now-minus-age-then identity, the integration bounds or hubble_time scaling is broken
checkers.scientific_quantity: age of the universe at a redshift, and lookback time (elapsed time since that redshift) -- related by age(0) - age(z) = lookback_time(z)

checkers.alarm: relative error between circstd's returned value and sqrt(-2*ln(1-circvar)) exceeds 1000*eps64
checkers.invariant: circstd(data, method='circular') == sqrt(-2*ln(1 - circvar(data))), computed via two independent public-API calls on the same data
checkers.observation_point: after circstd(method='circular') returns, re-calling the independent circvar() on the same input
checkers.precondition: 1D circular data (radians or angle Quantity), n>=2, circvar(data) < 1 (nonzero resultant length -- R=0 makes the log diverge)
checkers.rationale: circvar and circstd are astropy's two published circular-dispersion statistics; a regression that edits one formula's constant without the matching edit to the other would silently give internally-inconsistent dispersion estimates depending on which function a caller uses
checkers.scientific_quantity: circular dispersion of directional data via the mean resultant length R: circvar = 1-R, circstd(circular) = sqrt(-2*ln(R))

checkers.alarm: relative error between the re-call's result and a*base+b exceeds 1e-8
checkers.invariant: biweight_location(a*x + b) == a*biweight_location(x) + b for any a>0, b real
checkers.observation_point: after biweight_location's scalar-return path (axis=None case) computes its result, re-calling it on an affine-transformed copy of the same input
checkers.precondition: 1D real array, n>=5, nonzero MAD (excludes the documented all-equal/MAD-clamped degenerate branch), a>0 (only the analytically-certain sign is checked)
checkers.rationale: biweight_location is astropy's primary robust-location estimator (used by SigmaClippedStats and downstream photometry code) specifically because it should not depend on an arbitrary choice of units or zero-point; a break in affine equivariance would mean a 'robust mean' silently depends on unit choice
checkers.scientific_quantity: biweight location, a robust M-estimator of central tendency built from median, MAD-scaled residuals, and a weighted sum

checkers.alarm: relative error between the re-call's result and a**2*base exceeds 1e-9
checkers.invariant: biweight_midvariance(a*x + b) == a**2 * biweight_midvariance(x) for any real a, b, with modify_sample_size forwarded identically to both calls
checkers.observation_point: after biweight_midvariance's scalar-return path computes its result, re-calling it on an affine-transformed copy with modify_sample_size forwarded
checkers.precondition: 1D array of size>=5; finite positive result/std/MAD; finite c>0; |median|/(min(c,1)*MAD)<=500. This bounds both median-subtraction cancellation (independent of c) and normalized-residual conditioning (stronger when c<1).
checkers.rationale: biweight_midvariance (via biweight_scale) is astropy's robust-dispersion estimator used in SigmaClippedStats.biweight_scale() for robust image/photometry statistics; a break here would mean an estimated noise level silently changes under a pure unit rescaling
checkers.scientific_quantity: biweight midvariance, a robust variance estimator built entirely from squared, scale-and-shift-normalized residuals

checkers.alarm: when max(|x|)<=1e4, bias/max(|mean|,1) exceeds 1e-8; or std_err relative error exceeds 5*eps64*n*max(1,|mean|/predicted_std_err)
checkers.invariant: bias == 0 exactly (the jackknife mean estimator is exactly unbiased) and std_err == sqrt(sum((x-xbar)**2)/(n*(n-1)))
checkers.observation_point: after jackknife_stats returns, checked only when the caller's statistic argument is np.mean by identity
checkers.precondition: 1-D finite float64 array with statistic=np.mean (identity check), max(|x|) <= 1e4 for the bias sub-check. Fixed 2026-09-15 (codex CLI black-box trial): added an explicit float64-only dtype gate -- a float32 input previously produced a float32-precision bias/std_err compared against this checker's float64-derived tolerance, guaranteeing a false trigger (numpy dtype-preservation, not an astropy defect).
checkers.rationale: verifying jackknife_stats against the one case with a known closed form is a strong, non-tautological check on the shared resampling/bias-correction machinery (jackknife_resampling, the (n-1)*(mean_jack_stat-stat_data) bias formula, and the standard-error formula) that also silently affects every other statistic passed through the same code, but can only be caught where the correct value is independently known
checkers.scientific_quantity: jackknife bias and standard error for the specific, analytically tractable case of statistic=np.mean

checkers.alarm: abs(array.sum() - 1.0) > 10*eps64, only when the pre-normalization sum was nonzero
checkers.invariant: after normalize(mode='integral'), array.sum() == 1 exactly to float64 rounding
checkers.observation_point: immediately after Kernel.normalize() executes, reading the pre-normalization sum and the freshly-computed post-normalization sum
checkers.precondition: mode='integral'; pre-normalization sum finite and nonzero (the zero-sum case is production code's own documented skip-division branch, not part of this law)
checkers.rationale: every convolution correctness guarantee downstream of normalize_kernel=True (flux conservation, NaN-interpolation weighting, every kernel class's own 'integrates to 1' docstring contract) is only as good as this exactness; nothing else in the test suite checks the cross-kernel-shape relationship directly
checkers.scientific_quantity: the discrete integral (sum) of a kernel array after mode='integral' normalization -- the total transmission/throughput of the filter

checkers.alarm: flux error exceeds max(50*eps64, 30*eps64*sqrt(array.size))*kernel_condition*max(1,max(abs(array)))
checkers.invariant: convolve(array, kernel, boundary='wrap', normalize_kernel=True).sum() == array.sum()
checkers.observation_point: immediately after convolve() computes its final result, re-summing the original array_internal and the result
checkers.precondition: boundary='wrap', normalize_kernel=True, no mask, finite input/kernel, kernel not larger than the array, nonzero kernel sum, and kernel L1/sum condition <= eps64^-1/2
checkers.rationale: flux conservation under PSF convolution is a basic physical requirement for any application treating convolution as an instrument/optics model; no existing test checks this general conservation law explicitly
checkers.scientific_quantity: total flux (sum over all pixels) of an array before and after convolution with a kernel normalized to unit integral, on a boundary with no flux leakage/injection

checkers.alarm: max direct/FFT disagreement exceeds 50*eps64*kernel_condition*max(1,kernel.size,log2(array.size))*max(1,max(abs(array)))
checkers.invariant: convolve(array, kernel, ...) and convolve_fft(array, kernel, ...) agree elementwise to float64 rounding
checkers.observation_point: end of convolve(), additionally calling convolve_fft() with matching forwarded arguments and comparing
checkers.precondition: finite input/kernel, boundary in {fill, wrap}, normalize_kernel=True, kernel not larger than the array, input size <=4096, nonzero kernel sum, and kernel L1/sum condition <= eps64^-1/2
checkers.rationale: convolve and convolve_fft are astropy's two primary user-facing convolution entry points, documented as interchangeable modulo performance and independently implemented (compiled C vs NumPy FFT); disagreement beyond rounding means at least one has a correctness bug no single-function round-trip check in this bank could otherwise detect
checkers.scientific_quantity: the discrete convolution of an array with a kernel, computed two structurally unrelated ways (direct C summation vs FFT-domain multiplication)

checkers.alarm: relative error exceeds 10*eps64 when the constant's own uncertainty==0.0 (derived-in-repo vintages), else 1e-6 (independently-published-literal vintages)
checkers.invariant: sigma_sb == 2*pi^5*k_B^4/(15*h^3*c^2), using h/k_B/c from the same vintage module sigma_sb was defined in
checkers.observation_point: immediately after Constant.__new__ constructs sigma_sb, reading h/k_B/c from the constructing module's own namespace (not the process-wide active config)
checkers.precondition: abbrev='sigma_sb', system='si'; siblings h/k_B/c present in the constructing vintage module's own namespace Fixed 2026-09-15 (codex CLI black-box trial): check_constant_relation now requires caller_globals['__name__'] to start with 'astropy.constants.codata' -- previously any module whose globals() happened to contain the sibling constant names (h/k_B/c, etc.) satisfied the dispatch, which a synthetic Constant(abbrev, ..., wrong_value, ...) constructed in an arbitrary module could spoof by manually assigning real siblings into that module's globals(). Confirmed exploitable and now fixed; the law is unchanged (same-vintage-module constant self-consistency), only the module-identity check is now non-spoofable.
checkers.rationale: guards against a maintainer hand-editing one of h/k_B/c/sigma_sb's literal without re-deriving sigma_sb; nothing else in the test suite checks this cross-constant relationship
checkers.scientific_quantity: Stefan-Boltzmann constant vs its closed-form Planck-radiation-law derivation from h, k_B, c

checkers.alarm: relative error exceeds 10*eps64 when uncertainty==0.0, else 1e-7
checkers.invariant: R == N_A * k_B, using N_A/k_B from the same vintage module R was defined in
checkers.observation_point: immediately after Constant.__new__ constructs R, reading N_A/k_B from the constructing module's own namespace
checkers.precondition: abbrev='R', system='si'; siblings N_A/k_B present in the constructing vintage module's own namespace Fixed 2026-09-15 (codex CLI black-box trial): check_constant_relation now requires caller_globals['__name__'] to start with 'astropy.constants.codata' -- previously any module whose globals() happened to contain the sibling constant names (h/k_B/c, etc.) satisfied the dispatch, which a synthetic Constant(abbrev, ..., wrong_value, ...) constructed in an arbitrary module could spoof by manually assigning real siblings into that module's globals(). Confirmed exploitable and now fixed; the law is unchanged (same-vintage-module constant self-consistency), only the module-identity check is now non-spoofable.
checkers.rationale: guards the same transcription-drift class as AP-CONST-001 on an independent 2-operand relation; nothing else checks the cross-constant relationship
checkers.scientific_quantity: molar gas constant vs N_A * k_B

checkers.alarm: relative error exceeds 10*eps64
checkers.invariant: e_esu == e_gauss == e*c*10, e_emu == e/10, exact in every CODATA vintage (no independently-published-literal regime exists for these three)
checkers.observation_point: immediately after Constant.__new__ constructs any of the three, reading e/c from the constructing module's own namespace
checkers.precondition: abbrev in {e_esu, e_emu, e_gauss}; siblings e/c present in the constructing vintage module's own namespace Fixed 2026-09-15 (codex CLI black-box trial): check_constant_relation now requires caller_globals['__name__'] to start with 'astropy.constants.codata' -- previously any module whose globals() happened to contain the sibling constant names (h/k_B/c, etc.) satisfied the dispatch, which a synthetic Constant(abbrev, ..., wrong_value, ...) constructed in an arbitrary module could spoof by manually assigning real siblings into that module's globals(). Confirmed exploitable and now fixed; the law is unchanged (same-vintage-module constant self-consistency), only the module-identity check is now non-spoofable.
checkers.rationale: e_esu/e_emu/e_gauss are independently-typed literals in source that could drift from e/c under a careless edit; this is the tightest, purely algebraic identity in this bank's constants candidates
checkers.scientific_quantity: elementary charge in three CGS-family unit systems vs the exact SI e/c conversion

checkers.alarm: relative error exceeds 10*eps64
checkers.invariant: M_x == GM_x / G, using GM_x/G from the same astro-constant module M_x was defined in
checkers.observation_point: immediately after Constant.__new__ constructs M_x, reading GM_x/G from the constructing module's own namespace
checkers.precondition: abbrev in {M_sun, M_jup, M_earth}; the constructing module must define a GM_x sibling with the same body suffix (iau2012 has none and is skipped) Fixed 2026-09-15 (codex CLI black-box trial): check_constant_relation now requires caller_globals['__name__'] to start with 'astropy.constants.codata' -- previously any module whose globals() happened to contain the sibling constant names (h/k_B/c, etc.) satisfied the dispatch, which a synthetic Constant(abbrev, ..., wrong_value, ...) constructed in an arbitrary module could spoof by manually assigning real siblings into that module's globals(). Confirmed exploitable and now fixed; the law is unchanged (same-vintage-module constant self-consistency), only the module-identity check is now non-spoofable.
checkers.rationale: IAU2015 itself computes M_x this way in-repo and states the error-propagation model in its own uncertainty formula; this candidate turns that stated intent into a live-checked invariant
checkers.scientific_quantity: planetary/solar mass vs GM_x / G, where GM_x is independently measured via orbital dynamics and G is the (far less precise) CODATA gravitational constant

checkers.alarm: absolute disagreement exceeds 1e-6 after mapping {standard, model, log} to bounded standard power; relative disagreement exceeds 1e-6 for normalization='psd'
checkers.invariant: power computed via method="fast" agrees with method="slow" (the exact direct-sum reference implementation) within fast's own documented FFT/extirpolation approximation budget
checkers.observation_point: end of lombscargle() in implementations/main.py, after the resolved-method result is computed, when the resolved method is "fast"
checkers.precondition: nterms=1, regular frequency grid, N*Nfreq <= 2,000,000; default LRA fast backend with eps<=5e-13; |weighted_mean(y)|/weighted_rms(y-mean)<=1e8 when centering; comparison restricted per frequency to weighted sinusoid design-matrix condition <=1e4 and abs(frequency)*ptp(t)<=1e8 phase cycles
checkers.rationale: six independently coded LombScargle implementations are documented to compute the identical scientific quantity; slow exists specifically as the exact reference the others approximate or restate
checkers.scientific_quantity: Lomb-Scargle periodogram power at a given frequency

checkers.alarm: abs(fap_single(z, N, norm, dH, dK) - fap) > 1e-9 (absolute)
checkers.invariant: fap_single(inv_fap_single(fap, N, norm, dH, dK), N, norm, dH, dK) == fap -- fap_single and inv_fap_single are independently coded algebraic inverses of each other, one closed form per normalization branch
checkers.observation_point: inside inv_fap_single, immediately before returning z, for scalar fap inputs
checkers.precondition: fap in (0,1), dK-dH==2, dK < N <= 1,000,000 Fixed 2026-09-15 (codex CLI black-box trial, follow-up deep-verification pass): added an explicit float64-only dtype gate on fap/z -- previously a float16 fap (e.g. via LombScargle.false_alarm_level(np.float16(...))) produced a float16-precision inv_fap_single result (1 - fap**2 rounding to exactly 1.0), compared against this checker's float64-derived tolerance, guaranteeing a false trigger. Same family as AP-STATS-004/AP-VIS-001/002/003.
checkers.rationale: the forward and inverse formulas for each normalization are separate function bodies that could drift out of algebraic agreement under an independent edit (e.g. a sign or exponent error in only one), silently corrupting the false-alarm-probability/level tools used for periodogram peak significance decisions
checkers.scientific_quantity: single-frequency false-alarm probability and its functional inverse, for the null-hypothesis periodogram power distribution

checkers.alarm: relative disagreement, computed against the actual propagated result and scaled by the working dtype's own eps, exceeds 50*working_eps
checkers.invariant: converting the propagating class's own result to variance space must agree with an independent re-derivation via VarianceUncertainty.propagate() called on the same operation, operands, and correlation
checkers.observation_point: end of NDUncertainty.propagate(), immediately before it returns, binary-operand branch only
checkers.precondition: binary arithmetic propagation (not the collapse branch), both operand uncertainty arrays present, propagating class is StdDevUncertainty or InverseVariance (never VarianceUncertainty itself), operand classes match
checkers.rationale: StdDevUncertainty, VarianceUncertainty, and InverseVariance are three separately-coded to_variance/from_variance closures sharing the same _propagate_add_sub/_propagate_multiply_divide skeleton; an edit to one class's transform or unit-conversion branch that breaks agreement with the others would silently give a caller a wrong uncertainty depending only on which representation class they chose
checkers.scientific_quantity: first-order Gaussian error propagation for add/subtract/multiply/divide, expressed in three interconvertible uncertainty representations (standard deviation, variance, inverse variance)

checkers.alarm: Euclidean distance between the original Cartesian point and its round-tripped reconstruction, relative to the point's own distance from the origin, exceeds 20*eps64
checkers.invariant: from_cartesian(to_cartesian(s)).to_cartesian() must return to the same 3D point as to_cartesian(s) itself
checkers.observation_point: end of SphericalRepresentation.to_cartesian(), immediately before it returns
checkers.precondition: distance > 0 (documents why lon/lat may legitimately differ after a round trip through the origin; the Cartesian-space comparison itself stays trivially exact at distance==0)
checkers.rationale: to_cartesian (ERFA s2p) and from_cartesian (ERFA p2s) are independently coded compiled trigonometric transforms, not the same formula run twice; every frame transform, separation calculation, and represent_as conversion in the package depends on this round trip holding
checkers.scientific_quantity: a point in 3D space expressed in spherical polar coordinates (longitude, latitude, distance) versus its Cartesian (x, y, z) representation

checkers.alarm: relative error in any of d_lon, d_lat, d_distance after the round trip exceeds 5*eps64
checkers.invariant: SphericalDifferential.represent_as(SphericalCosLatDifferential, base).represent_as(SphericalDifferential, base) must return to the original differential
checkers.observation_point: inside SphericalDifferential.represent_as, immediately after constructing the SphericalCosLatDifferential result, before returning it
checkers.precondition: base given; d_lon * cos(base.lat) does not underflow below float64's smallest normal value (~2.23e-308)
checkers.rationale: the d_lon <-> d_lon_coslat conversion (multiply/divide by cos(base.lat)) is an exact algebraic inverse pair, but implemented as two separate methods (_d_lon_coslat on the source class, _get_d_lon as a classmethod on the target class) that could drift out of agreement under an independent edit to either
checkers.scientific_quantity: proper-motion/radial-velocity differential of a point in spherical coordinates, expressed with or without cos(lat) folded into the longitude component
checkers.symbol: SphericalDifferential.represent_as (SphericalCosLatDifferential branch; re-derives via SphericalCosLatDifferential.represent_as back to SphericalDifferential)

checkers.alarm: mad_std's own result differs at all (zero tolerance) from MAD*SMAD_SCALE_FACTOR recomputed with the other module's literal
checkers.invariant: astropy.stats.funcs's hardcoded literal (1.482602218505602) and astropy.uncertainty.core.SMAD_SCALE_FACTOR (1.48260221850560203193936104071326553821563720703125) must be the identical float64 value
checkers.observation_point: end of mad_std(), immediately before it returns
checkers.precondition: none -- a hardcoded-literal comparison
checkers.rationale: two independently-typed decimal literals for the same constant, in two different subsystems with no shared source, is the same transcription-drift risk the AP-CONST-* family guards against for physical constants
checkers.scientific_quantity: the constant 1/Phi^-1(3/4) ~= 1.4826, used to rescale the median absolute deviation into a standard-deviation estimate

checkers.alarm: the signed relative disagreement differs from beta/2 + beta^2/2 by more than 1e-6
checkers.invariant: V_opt/c = sqrt((1+beta)/(1-beta)) - 1 = beta + beta^2/2 + O(beta^3), so the optical-vs-relativistic relative disagreement is +beta/2 at leading order (same magnitude, opposite sign, as AP-UNITS-002's radio-vs-relativistic -beta/2)
checkers.observation_point: inside doppler_optical(), re-calling the public doppler_relativistic() for the same rest frequency at signed redshift and blueshift probes spanning the beta precondition window
checkers.precondition: rest frequency magnitude in [16*sqrt(float64_min_normal), sqrt(float64_max)/16], and |beta| in (1e-5,1e-3), identical to AP-UNITS-002's numerical domain
checkers.rationale: same as AP-UNITS-002 for the third Doppler convention: if the documented leading-order relationship breaks down, downstream velocity calibrations that assume this equivalence silently diverge from the claimed physics
checkers.scientific_quantity: radial velocity inferred from a Doppler-shifted spectral line, under the optical vs. relativistic naming conventions

checkers.alarm: relative error exceeds 1e-9
checkers.invariant: muB == e*hbar/(2*m_e), using e/hbar/m_e from the same vintage module muB was defined in
checkers.observation_point: immediately after Constant.__new__ constructs muB, reading e/hbar/m_e from the constructing module's own namespace
checkers.precondition: abbrev='muB', system='si'; siblings e/hbar/m_e present in the constructing vintage module's own namespace Fixed 2026-09-15 (codex CLI black-box trial): check_constant_relation now requires caller_globals['__name__'] to start with 'astropy.constants.codata' -- previously any module whose globals() happened to contain the sibling constant names (h/k_B/c, etc.) satisfied the dispatch, which a synthetic Constant(abbrev, ..., wrong_value, ...) constructed in an arbitrary module could spoof by manually assigning real siblings into that module's globals(). Confirmed exploitable and now fixed; the law is unchanged (same-vintage-module constant self-consistency), only the module-identity check is now non-spoofable.
checkers.rationale: same transcription-drift risk as AP-CONST-001/002/004 -- muB is an independently-published literal that could silently drift from its own derivable cross-constant relation under an uncoordinated edit to e, hbar, m_e, or muB itself
checkers.scientific_quantity: the Bohr magneton, derivable from three other fundamental constants: muB = e*hbar/(2*m_e)

checkers.alarm: max component-wise absolute error after the round trip, relative to max(|x|,|y|), exceeds 30*eps64
checkers.invariant: rotating (x, y) by angle then by -angle returns to (x, y)
checkers.observation_point: inside Rotation2D.evaluate, immediately after computing the forward-rotated (x, y), before returning it
checkers.precondition: finite angle, finite (x, y) -- no degenerate cases, a 2D rotation matrix is invertible for every angle
checkers.rationale: Rotation2D.inverse constructs a fresh model with angle=-self.angle, and evaluate() independently recomputes cos(-angle)/sin(-angle) via _compute_matrix rather than merely negating the forward matrix, so this is a genuine two-computation round trip; Rotation2D is used throughout astropy.modeling's compound-model machinery including WCS/gwcs pipelines
checkers.scientific_quantity: a 2D point rotated by an angle and then by the negated angle -- the modeling-framework analog of AP-COORD-002's frame-transform matrix round trip

checkers.alarm: max absolute error after the round trip exceeds 1000*eps64
checkers.invariant: InvertedLogStretch(a)(LogStretch(a)(x)) recovers x to within tolerance
checkers.observation_point: inside LogStretch.__call__, immediately after computing the forward-stretched result, before returning it
checkers.precondition: 1e-2 <= a <= 1e6, x in [0, 1], float64 x_in and y_out. Fixed 2026-09-15 (codex CLI black-box trial): added an explicit float64-only dtype gate on both x_in and y_out (checked before the checker's own dtype=float cast, which would otherwise erase the evidence) -- float32 input silently produces a float32-precision LogStretch result compared against this checker's float64-derived tolerance.
checkers.rationale: LogStretch computes y = log(a*x+1)/log(a+1); InvertedLogStretch computes the algebraically distinct closed form x = ((a+1)^y - 1)/a via exp/log rather than merely undoing LogStretch's own operations in reverse -- a genuine two-independently-computed-formula round trip, unlike the algebraic-cancellation round trips excluded elsewhere in this bank (e.g. RotateNative2Celestial/RotateCelestial2Native, EulerAngleRotation.inverse, which reduce to the same rotation matrix negated/reversed)
checkers.scientific_quantity: an image intensity value stretched by LogStretch(a) then restored by its own .inverse (InvertedLogStretch(a)) -- the first sanitizer in astropy.visualization

checkers.alarm: max absolute error after the round trip exceeds 100*eps64
checkers.invariant: SinhStretch(a'=1/asinh(1/a))(AsinhStretch(a)(x)) recovers x to within tolerance
checkers.observation_point: inside AsinhStretch.__call__, immediately after computing the forward-stretched result, before returning it
checkers.precondition: a >= 1e-10, x in [0, 1], float64 x_in and y_out. Fixed 2026-09-15 (codex CLI black-box trial): same float64-only dtype gate as AP-VIS-001, same rationale.
checkers.rationale: AsinhStretch computes y = asinh(x/a)/asinh(1/a); the inverse computes x = a'*sinh(y/a') via a rescaled parameter -- an algebraically distinct transcendental-function pair (asinh/log-family vs sinh/exp-family), the same genuine two-independently-computed-formula structure as AP-VIS-001, unlike this bank's tautological rotation round trips (RotateNative2Celestial/RotateCelestial2Native, EulerAngleRotation.inverse) which recompute the same trig formula with negated/reversed angles
checkers.scientific_quantity: an image intensity value stretched by AsinhStretch(a) then restored by its own .inverse (SinhStretch with rescaled a'=1/asinh(1/a))

checkers.alarm: max absolute error after the round trip exceeds 1000*eps64
checkers.invariant: InvertedPowerDistStretch(a)(PowerDistStretch(a)(x)) recovers x to within tolerance
checkers.observation_point: inside PowerDistStretch.__call__, immediately after computing the forward-stretched result, before returning it
checkers.precondition: 1e-3 <= |a| <= 1e3, |a-1| >= 1e-2, x in [0, 1], float64 x_in and y_out. Fixed 2026-09-15 (codex CLI black-box trial): same float64-only dtype gate as AP-VIS-001, same rationale.
checkers.rationale: PowerDistStretch computes y = (a^x-1)/(a-1); InvertedPowerDistStretch computes the algebraically distinct closed form x = log(y*(a-1)+1)/log(a) via a different transcendental-function family (power/exp vs log) -- the same genuine cross-check structure as AP-VIS-001 (LogStretch) and AP-VIS-002 (AsinhStretch)
checkers.scientific_quantity: an image intensity value stretched by PowerDistStretch(a) then restored by its own .inverse (InvertedPowerDistStretch(a))

checkers.alarm: relative Cartesian round-trip distance (distance / geocentric radius) exceeds 1e-9
checkers.invariant: EarthLocation.from_geodetic(EarthLocation.to_geodetic(loc)) recovers loc's Cartesian position to within tolerance
checkers.observation_point: inside EarthLocation.to_geodetic, immediately after computing the resulting lon/lat/height, before returning them
checkers.precondition: finite geocentric (x, y, z), and geocentric radius >= 4,000,000 m (excludes the near-Earth-center regime where ERFA's ellipsoid-inversion gc2gde is ill-conditioned)
checkers.rationale: to_geodetic uses ERFA's gc2gde (an ellipsoid-inversion algorithm); from_geodetic uses ERFA's gd2gce (a closed-form formula) -- a genuine two-independently-computed-algorithm round trip, comparable in trust level to this bank's other ERFA-backed checks (AP-WCS-001). Compared in Cartesian space (same convention as AP-COORD-005) to sidestep angle-wrap and pole-degeneracy entirely
checkers.scientific_quantity: a geocentric Cartesian position converted to geodetic lon/lat/height and back to geocentric Cartesian
